coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Kiribati scrap-dealer licensing or scrap export regime found (search returned only Kenya/Botswana/etc.). Scrap metal is explicitly outside the Special Fund (Waste Material Recovery) Act 2004 deposit scheme, which covers PET bottles, aluminium cans and lead-acid batteries; the 2025 Regulations (gazette, signed 29 Aug 2025) only set a customs-collected deposit (paid with import duty, no separate return) and let the Minister engage one waste recovery operator. Nothing to build for dealers. Source: https://www.president.gov.ki/images/Gazettes/2025/Special_Fund_Waste_Material_Recovery_Regulations_2025.pdf ; https://www.sprep.org/node/17588

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Kiribati second-hand dealer or pawnbroker statute surfaced (only NZ/Australia results). The only lending-type licence seen is the Moneylenders Act (Registrar licenses each business address annually, licences expire 31 Dec); that is a lender duty, not second-hand/pawn, and is likely a small number of operators. No evidence of a police register regime.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler licensing found. Solid-waste programme material says end-of-life vehicle (ELV) recycling was proposed to be added to the deposit/refund system but was NOT formally agreed by government; imports about 1,200 cars/yr, stockpile of ELVs growing; cabinet paper reported endorsed in 2018 (SPREP). The 2025 Special Fund Regulations do not mention vehicles. Watch item only: a future ELV levy/registration would hit importers and scrappers. Sources: https://www.sprep.org/node/17588 ; https://uncrd.un.org/sites/uncrd.un.org/files/12th3r_ps7-1-p2.pdf

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Only the Biosecurity Act 2011 (border control, import permits issued by MELAD Agriculture and Livestock Division, free, valid 3 months personal / 6 months commercial). No domestic livestock trader register, market or animal-movement regime found. Sources: https://pacliirms.paclii.org/ki/legis/num_act/ba2011156 ; https://kiribati.tradeportal.org (import permit procedures).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No abattoir or butcher licensing found. Food Act (Food Safety Act) 2006 and Food Regulations and Standards 2014 cover food business hygiene and premises closure; a WHO-facilitated multisectoral review of the Act and Regulations began June 2024 (possible future rule change, nothing enacted found). Pig slaughter is mostly household/community; no formal sector evident. Sources: https://pacliirms.austlii.edu.au/ki/legis/num_act/fsa2006127 ; https://www.who.int/guam/news-room/photo-story/photo-story-detail/who-supports-kiribati-to-employ-a-one-health-approach-to-advancing-food-safety

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No private veterinary sector or vet-medicine seller regime found; animal health is run by MELAD Agriculture and Livestock Division. Not applicable in practice.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No well-drilling or abstraction permit regime found. SPREP-hosted document states there is no comprehensive law on ownership, management and protection of water resources; Public Utilities Ordinance vests water-reserve protection in the Public Utilities Board. Groundwater is freshwater lens; wells are household/village. Sources: https://kiribati-data.sprep.org/resource/18/download/file ; https://pacliirms.paclii.org/ki/legis/consol_act/puo246

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No desludging or septic hauler licensing found. Sanitation sits under Public Health Ordinance 1926 and PUB standards; very few regulations in force; South Tarawa Sanitation Project (World Bank, MISE/PUB, stakeholder plan April 2025) is donor/state system building, out of scope for a private product. Sources: https://www.mise.gov.ki/sites/default/files/2026-03/Kiribati%20Stakeholders%20Engagement%20Plan%20V5_0.pdf

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing new. Water supply is PUB (state utility) on South Tarawa; outer islands village systems with no operator registers found. No regulatory reporting duty on small private systems found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No Kiribati pesticides act or dealer/applicator register found (a FAOLEX 'Pesticides Act' hit was for the Cook Islands). Only the generic MELAD biosecurity import permit. Tiny agricultural input market. Not confirmed either way.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No burial/cemetery/funeral regulation found (searches returned Kenya/NZ). Burial is village/church/family based; local councils under Local Government Act 1984 may have bye-laws (unverified). Nothing to build.

result.reason: Duty is real: the Tourism Act 2018 and the 2022 Tourism Operator's Registration and Licensing Regulation require accommodation and tour operators to register and pay annual licence fees to TAK. TAK notices give 2023 and 2025 as start dates, and I could not confirm the handover happened. No online portal or competing software turned up, but only two searches ran. I found no fee schedule, no guest-register or monthly-return duty, and no operator count. The market is a few dozen firms with one annual renewal, so there is almost nothing to build or sell. The buyers are also poor and hard to reach. Not worth pursuing.

decisions.reason: Guest houses/lodges/tour operators owe annual TAK registration and licence; new buyer group and duty, not in known.
Kava bars/retailers/wholesalers have recurring Kava Act licensing and sales-hour duties; new buyer and duty.
Fish processors/exporters owe annual licence renewal plus per-consignment quality certificates; different duty from K01 catch logbooks, so a new candidate (related K01).
Copra buyers/co-ops must keep a purchase register and pay monthly copra tax; new buyer and duty, unverified.
Co-operative societies owe annual returns and audit to the Registrar; in-scope body, duty unverified.
Crewing agencies are small firms with MLC/contract duties; trigger unclear but unverified, not rejected.
Private pharmacies/importers have medicine licence and register duties under Medicines Act; small professional offices in scope.
Licensed premises owe Liquor Ordinance licence renewals and compliance; new buyer and duty.
Shops and traders owe annual council operational licence renewals; new buyer and duty.
Importers of controlled goods need import licences under the Price Control Act 2023; differs from K02 customs declarations (related K02), unverified.
Builders and trades face new registration and permit duties under the Building Act 2024; new buyer and duty.
Churches and societies have registration and register duties; community and religious bodies are in scope.
Not a current mandatory duty: the levy is only a proposal, not agreed and not in the 2025 Regulations, so there is no recurring workflow to serve.
